title: Microsoft Teams Shifts: Assign open shifts fills open shifts automatically
summary: Hold: the prescribed PowerShell blocking value conflicts with its reference page, which labels that example as unblocking an app. The statement that there is no spending cap also goes beyond the verified absence of a published meter. The scheduling behaviour, Teams licence requirement and rollout information are supported, with smaller corrections needed for conflicting control documentation and missing citations.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked $true is the documented PowerShell call to block the app.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Replace the call in both representations with 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean>'. Add to the note: 'The reference describes IsBlocked as the app state, but labels examples using both $true and $false as unblocking. Use the documented Status toggle for a Blocked or Allowed choice until Microsoft clarifies the examples.' Do not claim the printed $true example is verified to block.

claims.claim: The cited Shifts management page says specific users can be allowed or blocked using a custom app permission policy assigned to them.
claims.quote: To allow or block specific users in your organization from using Shifts, make sure Shifts is turned on for your organization on the Manage apps page. Then create a custom policy for app permissions and assign it to those users.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'For organisations still using app permission policies, Learn says specific users can be allowed or blocked by creating a custom app permission policy and assigning it to them; Shifts must be allowed at the org level. Microsoft says permission policies no longer apply after moving to app-centric management.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-app-permission-policies to sources; its Important note states that qualification.
